items.name: avatar
items.title: Blobatar
items.description: An Avatar that falls back to a deterministic geometric blobatar generated from the user's name.
items.author: Alain <https://blobatar.dev>
items.//dependencies: Unpinned on purpose. Every package in this set publishes the same version, so `latest` of both resolves to a matched pair — which is what `@blobatar/react`'s exact-major peer range on `blobatar` requires. A `^2` written here would instead freeze this item at gen2 the moment gen3 ships, and a registry item nobody rebuilds is exactly how that goes unnoticed.

items.name: presence-avatar
items.title: Presence avatar
items.description: A blobatar with a presence dot and an unread badge. Online, away, offline, and a thinking state, on a face that blinks and breathes.
items.author: Alain <https://blobatar.dev>
items.//docs: The thinking state is the only part of any item here that needs a stylesheet, and it fails silently without one: the face is correct and simply holds still. Said in `docs` rather than only in the file's header comment because the CLI prints this after installing, which is the moment it is actionable.
items.docs: Every face animates. Import the library's stylesheet once, anywhere in your app: `import "blobatar/motion.css"`.

items.name: agent-list
items.title: Agent list
items.description: A sidebar group of running agents, each with a face derived from its name, a presence dot and a line of what it is doing. Drops into shadcn's Sidebar.
items.author: Alain <https://blobatar.dev>
items.//registryDependencies: `sidebar` is shadcn's own, by bare name, so it resolves against whatever registry the installing project has configured as its default. The other is a full URL rather than `@blobatar/presence-avatar`: the namespace form only resolves in a project that has run `shadcn registry add @blobatar=...`, and the README also hands out `Alain00/blobatar/agent-list`, which registers nothing. A URL resolves under both.
items.docs: Render it inside your `SidebarProvider`, in the sidebar you already have. Every row's face animates, so import the library's stylesheet once, anywhere in your app: `import "blobatar/motion.css"`.

items.name: user-table
items.title: User table
items.description: A table of people with a blobatar per row, rendered as static images so that a long list stays one node per face.
items.author: Alain <https://blobatar.dev>

items.name: group-chat
items.title: Group chat
items.description: A thread with several people in it: consecutive messages grouped under one face, an overlapping facepile, and a typing indicator.
items.author: Alain <https://blobatar.dev>
items.docs: The avatars react on hover. Import the library's stylesheet once, anywhere in your app: `import "blobatar/motion.css"`.

items.name: password-field
items.title: Password field
items.description: A password input with a face above it. It watches the caret while you type, and goes sleepy when you reveal what you typed.
items.author: Alain <https://blobatar.dev>
items.//docs: The only item that needs two stylesheets, and the second one fails silently in the way that matters most here: without `gaze.css` the face is correct, blinks and breathes, and simply never looks at anything, which reads as the component being broken rather than as a missing import.
items.docs: The face animates and follows the caret. Import both stylesheets once, anywhere in your app: `import "blobatar/motion.css"` and `import "blobatar/gaze.css"`.
